import html from typing import List # Example template. In real use this should be imported from the project. USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{headline}

By: {poster_name}

{text}
{tags}
""" def compose_post_html( poster_name: str, headline: str, text: str, hashtags: List[str] ) -> str: """ Build an XSS‑safe HTML representation of a forum post. Parameters ---------- poster_name : str Name of the author. headline : str Post headline/title. text : str Main content of the post. hashtags : list[str] List of tags; each will be wrapped in a . Returns ------- str The HTML string ready for display. Raises ------ TypeError If any argument is not of the expected type. """ # Basic type checks if not isinstance(poster_name, str): raise TypeError("poster_name must be a string") if not isinstance(headline, str): raise TypeError("headline must be a string") if not isinstance(text, str): raise TypeError("text must be a string") if not (isinstance(hashtags, list) and all(isinstance(t, str) for t in hashtags)): raise TypeError("hashtags must be a list of strings") # Escape all user‑supplied content safe_poster = html.escape(poster_name, quote=True) safe_headline = html.escape(headline, quote=True) safe_text = html.escape(text) # Build tags string tag_spans = " ".join(f'{html.escape(tag, quote=True)}' for tag in hashtags) safe_tags = html.escape(tag_spans) # escape the whole string to avoid accidental markup # Populate template return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( poster_name=safe_poster, headline=safe_headline, text=safe_text, tags=safe_tags )
